Resort On Yu Yuen Rd.
Said Most Lavish
In Entire City

Repeated official promises that
local gambling dens in the west-
ern area would be reduced, showed
even more remote chance of fulfill-
ment today, when it was learned
that one more gaming house was
opened last night at 736 Yu Yuen
Road, while another is likely to

foreign club in the Settlement.
The new gambling den on Yu

with its lights brightly illuminat-

most lavish of its kind so far
established in the western area.

stakes at the new gambling den
are high and only persons with
special passes will be permitted to
enter and play at the tables.

Bubbling Well Road.

October 23, 1940.
Afternoon. Translation

Cheng Yien Pao :-

"SINO-JAPANESE ECONOMIC RESEARCH ASSOCIATION' IS AN OPIUM
AND GAMBLING ORGANIZATION"

On October 14, Ting Kuo-hwa (丁國華),
responsible member of the "Sino Japanese Economic Research
Association" (中日經濟研究會) at No. 82 Yates Road, sent
Zien Yang-yuan (錢養元) and Liu Ming-sung (劉明生),
two accountants, to take 128 ounces of opium to the Jcu Kong
dyes shop (瑞康顏料號) at House No. 10, Lane 277,
Shantung Road, and to hand the drug to one Wu (吳), an
accountant of the shop. Zien and Liu were instructed by
Ting to go by motor car, Licence No. 9118, which is owned by
Li Jeu-kiu (李玖), grandson of Marquis Li Hung-chang,
residing at No. 150 Edinburgh Road. The motor car was
driven by chauffeur Zau Peng-sung (曹奉生).
When the car arrived at the entrance of
Lane 277 Shantung Road, the opium was discovered by officers
of the Narcotic Section of the Shanghai Municipal Police.
Zien, Liu, and Zau were taken to the Police Station together
with the motor car and the opium. When the officers went
to arrest Wu, he had already made good his escape. The
arrested persons were later charged in the Shanghai First
Special District Court.

Yesterday morning, a further hearing of
the case was held by Judge Sin-feng (辛豐).
Mr. Paul Hu, Municipal Advocate, stated
that House No. 82 Yates Road is a large secret gambling den
which is also engaged in opium traffic. The opium seized
was sold to the Jcu Kong dyes shop. As Wu has escaped,
the Court would be requested in accordance with law to issue
a warrant for his arrest. Mr. Paul Hu further stated that
the motor car Licence No. 9118 had been taken away from the
Police Station by a Japanese. He then requested, under
Article 5 of the Opium Suppression Law, that a penalty be
imposed upon the accused.

Accused Zien Yang-yuan stated that he did
not know anything about the sending of opium.
Accused Liu Ming-sung stated that he sent
the opium to the Jcu Kong dyes shop under instructions from
Ting Kuo-hwa.
Accused Zau Peng-sung stated that the car
he drove belonged to one Lee and had been sent to House No. 82
Yates Road, and that he was ordered to drive the car to
Shantung Road on that day but he did not know that opium
was being transported.

Judge Sino announced that the accused
Zien Yang-yuan and Liu Peng-sung, for having engaged in
trafficking in opium, would each be sentenced to five
years' imprisonment, in addition to a fine of $1,000 each,
and be deprived of civil rights for five years; that the
accused Zau Peng-sung, for a similar offence, would be
sentenced to two and a half years' imprisonment, in
addition to being deprived of civil rights for two years;
that the 128 ounces of seized opium be confiscated.

P. T. O.

1940年10月23日。
下午。译文

《诚言报》：

“中日经济研究会”是鸦片与赌博组织

10月14日，叶茨路（Yates Road，即今淮海中路一段或附近，需结合当时地名，Yates Rd通常为霞飞路部分或独立路段，此处保留原文或通用译名，若不确定则保留）82号“中日经济研究会”负责人丁国华（Ting Kuo-hwa），派遣两名会计师钱养元（Zien Yang-yuan）和刘明生（Liu Ming-sung），将128两鸦片送往山东路277弄10号的瑞康颜料号（Jcu Kong dyes shop，原文Jcu Kong对应瑞康），并交给该店的一名吴姓（Wu）会计师。丁国华指示钱、刘二人乘坐牌照号为9118的汽车前往，该车归居住在爱丁堡路150号的李鸿章之孙李玖（Li Jeu-kiu）所有。司机为曹奉生（Zau Peng-sung）。
当汽车到达山东路277弄口时，上海公共租界工部局警务处禁毒科警官发现了鸦片。钱、刘和曹连同汽车及鸦片被带往警察局。当警官前去逮捕吴某时，他已逃脱。被捕人员随后在上海第一特区地方法院被起诉。

昨天上午，辛丰法官（Judge Sin-feng）对该案进行了进一步审理。
公诉人胡保罗先生（Mr. Paul Hu）指出，叶茨路82号是一个大型秘密赌窟，同时也从事鸦片交易。被查获的鸦片是出售给瑞康颜料号的。由于吴某在逃，将依法请求法院签发逮捕令。胡保罗先生还指出，牌照号为9118的汽车已被一名日本人从警察局取走。随后，他根据《禁烟法》第五条，请求对被告处以刑罚。

被告钱养元称，他对运送鸦片一事毫不知情。
被告刘明生称，他是受丁国华指示将鸦片送往瑞康颜料号的。
被告曹奉生称，他驾驶的汽车属于一位李姓人士，曾被派往叶茨路82号，当天他奉命将车开往山东路，但他不知道车上运输的是鸦片。

辛法官宣布，被告钱养元和刘鹏生（原文为Liu Peng-sung，与前文Liu Ming-sung不符，照实译出）因从事鸦片贩卖，各判处五年有期徒刑，并处罚金各1000元，剥夺公权五年；被告曹奉生犯有类似罪行，判处二年六个月有期徒刑，并剥夺公权二年；查获的128两鸦片予以没收。

Chinese-American Daily News, National Herald, Cheng Yien Pao,
Sin Wen Pao and Shun Pao :-

C.P.C. FATALLY SHOOTS C.D.C. BY MISTAKE

The Dah Sing Clock and Watch Shop (大新鐘表行),
No. 230 Kiukiang Road and Hupeh Road, next to the New Wei
Chung Hotel (新惠中花会), is owned by Koo Pao-shu (顧宝樹),
a native of Ningpo. This shop has been robbed three times
this year: once on January 6, the second time in March and
yesterday was the third time.
At about 7 p.m. yesterday, three robbers, two of
whom were armed with pistols, entered the shop and after xx
intimidating the inmates, robbed the place of 49 watches
valued at $1,600. The robbers decamped along Kiukiang Road
in an easterly direction.
When nearing Kiu King Lee (裘錦里), Shanse
Road, the robbers were met by C.P.C. 424 of Louza Station
who gave chase to the men and opened fire at them.
At about this time, Central Police Station
received an alarm and sent out a number of armed Chinese and
foreign detectives and policemen in a car. Chinese Detective
Chin Tuh-sun (金德勝) gave chase to the robbers. As the
C.D.C. who was in plain clothes was running close to the
robbers, the C.P.C. mistook him for one of the robbers and
fired four shots at him. One shot struck the C.D.C. in the
back of his head and emerged through the forehead. He fell
down in front of the Chang Shing Kee Silk Thread Shop
(長興記) in Kiu King Lee. A C.P.C. on duty nearby sent
the wounded C.D.C. to the Lester Chinese Hospital in a car,
but the officer succumbed to his wounds at 8 p.m.
The robbers made good their escape.
A stray bullet broke a glass in the showcase of
the Sze Shing Chong Embroidery Shop (時新昌).

Cheng Yien Pao :-

JOINT MEETING TO BE HELD BY VARIOUS BENEVOLENT BODIES TO-MORROW

Of late contributions received for refugee
relief have shown a marked decrease. A meeting of various
benevolent bodies was summoned last week by the Shanghai
Refugee Relief Association at which it was decided that all
young and able-bodied refugees in the various refugee camps
should be given a sum of money and be repatriated; that the
rest of the refugees be kept in four camps.
However, some of the refugee camps are opposed to

the young and able-bodied refugees have been repatriated, the

easier to manage the refugees and the expenses could be
curtailed. It is learned that a joint meeting of representatives
of the various benevolent bodies will be convened to-morrow

there will be some changes in refugee relief work in Shanghai
will be decided at the meeting to-morrow.

The China Press
SHANGHAI, THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 26, 1940
I'VE OFTEN WONDERED BY CARROLL D. ALCOTT

Gambling Den
I HAVE received, during the past few days, numerous telephone calls complaining against the operation of a certain gambling den in the International Settlement of Shanghai.
This den, according to all accounts, is a fly-by-night affair. But it seems to have been well patronized for reports concerning its existence have been in circulation for some time.
The argument presented by those complaining was quite simple. They contended that since complaints against the gambling houses in the badlands have been common, it was only fair that mention should be made of this particular spot.
In this column, on the morning of September 21, I made mention of the establishment. I stated:
"Part of the revenue taken in by one of the local gambling dens is reported to be finding its way into the Italian war chest . . . Although the police know of the existence of the place, they are almost powerless to do anything about it. The den operates under the protection of a certain foreign nation which has extrality rights in China. If the police want to raid the place, a warrant is needed from the consular authorities concerned. While this may be forthcoming, news of the impending raid somehow gets into the hands of the operators and all the gaming equipment is removed before the police have a chance to get on the spot."
The Italian authorities have complained to the Shanghai Municipal Council, claiming that this report was malignant. I would like to point out, however, that my statement did not involve the Italian authorities. I merely said that it was reported that some of the revenue was finding its way into the hands of the Italian war chest. I presume that if anyone wants to donate to the Italian war chest, no matter how he got the money, that is his business.
As far as I know, the Italian authorities have nothing to do with the place, nor did I say they had. They may not even know of its existence, nor did I accuse them of knowing anything about it. If this is the impression created, I regret that such a misunderstanding should have developed.
Regarding the assertion that the "den operates as a club under the protection of a certain foreign nation which has extrality rights in China," this assertion is an error. Those allegedly concerned are foreigners but they no longer have extrality rights. They did up to a few years ago. As far as the location of this establishment is concerned, I shall name the place over the air when I have completed my own investigations.

上海，1940年9月26日，星期四
卡罗尔·D·奥尔科特（CARROLL D. ALCOTT）撰：《我常常在想》

赌场
在过去几天里，我接到了无数电话，投诉上海公共租界内某家赌场的运营。
据各方说法，这家赌场是一家朝不保夕的机构。但似乎光顾者众多，因为关于其存在的报道已流传了一段时间。
投诉者提出的理由很简单。他们声称，既然对不良地带赌房的投诉司空见惯，那么提及这个特定地点也是公平的。
在9月21日上午的本专栏中，我提到了该场所。我当时说：
“据报道，本地一家赌场的部分收入正流入意大利战争基金……尽管警方知道该地方的存在，但他们几乎无能为力。该赌场在某个在华享有治外法权的外国国家的庇护下运营。如果警方想要突袭该地，需要从相关领事当局获得搜查令。虽然搜查令可能会下发，但即将突袭的消息不知何故传到了经营者手中，在警方有机会到达现场之前，所有赌博设备已被移除。”
意大利当局已向上海公共租界工部局投诉，声称该报道具有恶意。然而，我想指出，我的陈述并未牵涉意大利当局。我只是说，据报道部分收入流入了意大利战争基金。我推测，如果有人想向意大利战争基金捐款，无论钱是如何得来的，那是他自己的事。
据我所知，意大利当局与该地方无关，我也未说过他们有关。他们甚至可能不知道其存在，我也未指责他们知情。如果造成了这种印象，我对产生这样的误解表示遗憾。
关于“该赌场作为俱乐部在某个在华享有治外法权的外国国家庇护下运营”的说法，这一断言是错误的。那些据称有关联的外国人已不再拥有治外法权。他们在几年前确实拥有。至于该场所的位置，待我完成自己的调查后，我将在广播中公布该地点名称。

Commissioner of Police.
Sir,

At 3 p.m., September 24, I interviewed Mr. G.
Leonoff, City Editor of the "China Press", relative to a
news item published on September 21 and which forms the
subject of complaint by the Acting Consul General for Italy.
Mr. Leonoff at once pronounced the news item to be the work
of Mr. Carroll Alcott and promised to bring the complaint
to the notice of Mr. Alcott. At 10 a.m., September 25,
Mr. Alcott telephoned to this office and asked what action
the Police expect him to take. He went on to explain
that the news item does not state that the gambling den
referred to is operated by an Italian subject and is prepared
to publish a further news item to this effect in the "China
Press" on September 26.

Mr. Alcott, in reply to further questions, stated
that the gambling den referred to is in an apartment on
Bubbling Well Road and that the Police have raided the
establishment on one occasion. He stated that the two
proprietors are Spanish citizens and that certain foreigners
resident in Shanghai are willing to testify that they have
gambled in the establishment under review. At this
juncture I suggested that a responsible Police Officer call
on Mr. Alcott this morning and obtain full particulars of the
evidence in his possession. He pleaded pressure of work and
secondly that he preferred to state his case in writing which
action he proposes to take on or before Friday, September 27.

SEP 26 1940
I'VE OFTEN WONDERED BY CARROLL D. ALCOTT

Gambling Den
I HAVE received, during the past few days, numerous telephone calls complaining against the operation of a certain gambling den in the International Settlement of Shanghai.
This den, according to all accounts, is a fly-by-night affair. But it seems to have been well patronized for reports concerning its existence have been in circulation for some time.
The argument presented by those complaining was quite simple. They contended that since complaints against the gambling houses in the badlands have been common, it was only fair that mention should be made of this particular spot.
In this column, on the morning of September 21, I made mention of the establishment. I stated:
"Part of the revenue taken in by one of the local gambling dens is reported to be finding its way into the Italian war chest . . . Although the police know of the existence of the place, they are almost powerless to do anything about it. The den operates under the protection of a certain foreign nation which has extrality rights in China. If the police want to raid the place, a warrant is needed from the consular authorities concerned. While this may be forthcoming, news of the impending raid somehow gets into the hands of the operators and all the gaming equipment is removed before the police have a chance to get on the spot."
The Italian authorities have complained to the Shanghai Municipal Council, claiming that this report was malignant. I would like to point out, however, that my statement did not involve the Italian authorities. I merely said that it was reported that some of the revenue was finding its way into the hands of the Italian war chest. I presume that if anyone wants to donate to the Italian war chest, no matter how he got the money, that is his business.
As far as I know, the Italian authorities have nothing to do with the place, nor did I say they had. They may not even know of its existence, nor did I accuse them of knowing anything about it. If this is the impression created, I regret that such a misunderstanding should have developed.
Regarding the assertion that the "den operates as a club under the protection of a certain foreign nation which has extrality rights in China," this assertion is an error. Those allegedly concerned are foreigners but they no longer have extrality rights. They did up to a few years ago. As far as the location of this establishment is concerned, I shall name the place over the air when I have completed my own investigations.

Portuguese Law
According to Portuguese law, you can't arrest
a man between dusk and sunup. Local police tell
me that this is one of the reasons why it is so
difficult to arrest any Portuguese who might be
engaged in operating a gambling den in Shanghai.

evade the law. They have the entire night in
which to make a getaway.

9月16日，一家名为“胜利公司”（Sung Li Company）的小型赌窟在爱丁堡路667号旁的一栋无门牌号码的房屋内成立，该处位于越界筑路区（O.O.L.）（乾坤戏院对面）。该赌窟每日向位于愚园路1032弄的东亚慈善协会缴纳费用200.00美元。

目前在西区以下地址运营的共有两家主要赌窟和四家小型赌窟：
